refuted.why:
Three independent defects, each fatal to the claim as stated.

(1) THE NAMED ESCAPE HATCH IS FICTIONAL. The claim is conditioned on "the forbidden filename join" being the alternative route. There is no such join. All 5056 `*.response.json` are named `req_<REQUEST_ID>.response.json`; 0 of 5064 `*.request.json` are named `req_*` (they are uuid4). The request JSON carries no request-id field at all — `jq -r 'keys[]'` over requests gives only `betas context_management diagnostics fallbacks max_tokens messages metadata model output_config stream system thinking tools`. Response top-level keys across ALL 5056 files are only `usage type stop_sequence stop_reason stop_details role model id content diagnostics`, and response `.diagnostics` is `null` in 5046 of 5056 and `{cache_miss_reason:…}` in the other 10 — no session, no request id. So the response filename cannot join to a request by filename OR by field, in either direction. A claim whose "only other way" could never have worked is not a bounded claim.

(2) THE BOUND'S RATIONALE IS EMPIRICALLY FALSE. "≤34 (one per conversation thread)" assumes at most one terminal response per thread. Four response ids in this very corpus are referenced by 2–3 different requests (5 surplus references), i.e. threads fork/retry, and each fork adds an extra tail: `msg_011CeJ9Rngv…`(2), `msg_011CeJhJbwY…`(2), `msg_011CeJiWSWD…`(2), `msg_011CeHxfUXd…`(3). 0 response ids are referenced across two sessions, so these are genuine intra-session forks.

(3) AN EXACT DERIVATION EXISTS FROM THE SAME FIELDS. `unreferenced_responses = null_prev_requests + duplicate_prevs − (requests − responses)` closes to the unit on two independent snapshots taken minutes apart: snapshot 1 → 425 + 5 − 8 = 422 predicted, 422 measured; snapshot 2 → 425 + 5 − 7 = 423 predicted, 423 measured. No filename join, no temporal reconstruction — only `.diagnostics.previous_message_id`, `.id`, `.metadata.user_id` and file counts. Applied per-session it yields a TWO-SIDED bound, not "only an upper bound": target session now has 1113 requests / 41 null-prev / 0 dups, and `missing` is ≤7 corpus-wide, so Class 2 ∈ [34, 41]; at any moment where `requests_total == responses_total` (observable from the same data) it collapses to the exact equality Class 2 = Class 1 + dup.

Also: the report's "34" is a snapshot of a LIVE sink that the validation lane itself is writing into (975→1113 requests, 34→41 null-prev between the report and this probe), so the figure is a property of a moment, not of the session.

CONTRADICTION WITH THE OTHER FINDINGS: finding 2 rests on the SAME fictional "forbidden filename join". That is not a contradiction but a shared-premise defect across two findings — both should be restated as "the sink provides no forward link whatsoever", which is stronger and true. Finding 1 is unaffected, though its "975 requests" scope figure has drifted to 1113 by the same live-sink growth.
